create.name: Jason Shulman
create.bio:
Jason Shulman, who also uses the Buddhist name Jinen, is an American teacher of nonduality whose work draws on both the Kabbalah and Buddhism. He founded A Society of Souls, a school of nondual healing and awakening, and its teachings all grow out of his own realisation that the personal self and the absolute are not two separate things. Rather than trying to get rid of the ego, his approach aims to heal it and bring it into a right relationship with the larger reality it belongs to.

The school's main training is Nondual Kabbalistic Healing, a four-year course that combines the Tree of Life and other Kabbalistic maps with Buddhist thought and Western psychology. Around it sit shorter practices he devised: Impersonal Movement, a moving meditation; the MAGI Process, an imaginal method for working with conflict; and the Nondual Shaman training. His books include Kabbalistic Healing, The Instruction Manual for Receiving God, Beyond the Now and The Nondual Shaman, and he has also recorded several albums of songs. The Foundation for Nonduality shares his talks and runs free online classes based on his methods.

courses.title: Nondual Kabbalistic Healing Training
courses.description: A Society of Souls' main programme, a four-year training that teaches sixteen healings drawing on the Tree of Life, the Four Universes, Buddhist thought and nondual understanding. New year-one classes open periodically in the United States and Europe.

courses.title: Impersonal Movement
courses.description: A moving meditation he developed to set up the conditions for experiencing the unitive state, taught in two parts that can be practised separately or together.

courses.title: The MAGI Process
courses.description: An imaginal meditation for working with inner and outer conflict from a nondual point of view, treating conflict as part of the spiritual path rather than something to avoid.

courses.title: The Nondual Shaman
courses.description: A contemporary shamanic training for awakening the self, built on his nondual teaching and offered through the school alongside his book of the same name.
